decisions.sentence: The table was read through the `clinical` lens.
`readmit_30d` was chosen as the outcome; it is measured on all `480` rows.
`1` of `readmit_30d` was taken as the event and coded 1; `0` was coded 0.
`readmit_30d` was analyzed as a yes/no outcome: everyone was followed for the same time, as answered, so it counts events over one period.
The analysis was declared for `inference`: associations are estimated with their uncertainty.
Each row was declared a different participant: no one appears in more than one row.

Column roles were set for `10` columns: exposure `albumin_g_dl`; covariates `age`, `sex`, `charlson_index` and 5 more; identifier `encounter_id`; `encounter_id` and `albumin_g_dl` were proposed below high confidence and wait for their own confirmation before any default reads them.
`encounter_id` was confirmed as an identifier, on its own, after the evidence for its reading was read.
`albumin_g_dl` was confirmed as an exposure, on its own, after the evidence for its reading was read.

Nothing groups the participants above the person; each is analyzed as independent; `sodium_mmol_l` and `length_of_stay_days` were asked whether they group the participants, and the answer was that they do not.
No rows were excluded: every row with `readmit_30d` measured stays in the analysis.
A complete-case analysis was applied: no row is missing any predictor, so all `480` rows remain.
No rows were held out: every analyzed row estimates the coefficients, and no cross-validated score is reported under inference: the declared model is reported by its estimates.

Column roles were set for `10` columns: predictors `age`, `sex`, `charlson_index` and 6 more; identifier `encounter_id`; `encounter_id` and `albumin_g_dl` were proposed below high confidence and wait for their own confirmation before any default reads them.

A complete-case analysis was applied: no row is missing any predictor, so all `480` rows remain.
